title: Add Vaporize JSON Schema fixture validation for schema-universal expected-pass and expected-fail records
createdBy: codex after chairman required a governed vaporware modification request

historicalContent.sourceLocation: Codex session 2026-07-04: chairman rejected jq as authoritative schema fixture proof and required an entire Vaporware Modification Request before implementation.
historicalContent.description: Vaporize needs a first-class JSON Schema fixture validation command so schema-backed release evidence can prove both expected-pass and expected-fail fixtures without ad hoc jq checks. The first proof set is schema-universal workstream-schemas v0.0.4, whose fixtures distinguish ongoing workstreams, temporary initiatives, summaries, and invalid lifecycle classifications.
acceptanceCriteria: Vaporize exposes validate-json-schema with --schema, --fixture, and --expect pass|fail.
The command exits 0 only when the actual schema validation result matches the declared expectation.
The command exits nonzero when the fixture fails an expected-pass check or unexpectedly passes an expected-fail check.
The command emits or can write a structured receipt naming schema path, fixture path, expectation, actual result, diagnostics, and next steps.
The implementation supports the local reference and draft vocabulary needs of workstream-schemas v0.0.4 before that fixture set is claimed as proved.
CUJ-06 Swift Testing coverage exercises JSON syntax validation, expected-pass schema validation, expected-fail schema validation, expectation mismatch, and actionable failure output.
No XCTest target is introduced for this slice.
Release evidence names the new schema-backed fixture validation obligation or explicitly records why release-doctor enforcement is deferred.
Every command error includes robust next steps, procedure or evidence links, and guidance to bring the error to Digikoma when the operator cannot proceed.
The prior jq semantic fixture check is not used as the authoritative release proof.
knownSeparations: This bead owns the Vaporize command and release proof lane, not the schema-universal workstream schema semantics.
schema-universal owns the schema files, fixture records, and schema migrator semantics.
The initial command may scope to local schemas and local references; remote schema fetching is not part of the first acceptance slice.
The existing validate-json repeated --path bug can be fixed alongside this work, but it is not a substitute for schema instance validation.
The bead is filed at the Vaporize owner home first; a job-board projection should reference this bead when a Vaporize implementation board is opened.
